definition: The player who is rolling the dice. The dice pass clockwise to a new shooter after a seven-out.
The dealer in the middle with the long stick. Calls each roll and runs the center bets.
The casino employee who sits between the two dealers and supervises the game.
A disc that is black OFF on one side and white ON on the other. It marks whether a point is set, and which one.
The first roll of a round, while the puck is OFF. 7 and 11 are naturals, 2, 3 and 12 are craps, anything else becomes the point.
The number (4, 5, 6, 8, 9 or 10) set by the come-out roll. The shooter must roll it again before a 7.
A 7 or 11 on the come-out. Pass Line bets win.
A 2, 3 or 12 on the come-out. Pass Line bets lose. Also the name of the game.
A 7 rolled while a point is set. The Pass Line loses and the dice move to the next shooter.
Rolling the point number again before a 7. The Pass Line wins.
A total made as a pair: 2-2, 3-3, 4-4 or 5-5. Any other way to make that total is easy.
Making 4, 6, 8 or 10 without a pair, such as 1-5 for a 6.
One specific outcome of the two dice. There are 36, each equally likely.
The main bet of the game. Wins on a come-out 7 or 11, loses on 2, 3 or 12, and otherwise rides on the point. Pays even money.
The opposite of the Pass Line. Wins on 2 or 3 (12 is a push) and when 7 comes before the point.
A bet you cannot take down once a point is set, such as the Pass Line after a point is set.
A 1:1 payout. Bet $10, win $10.
The average result of a bet per dollar over the long run. Almost every bet is negative.
The negative of EV, as a percentage of the money bet. The Pass Line's is 1.41%.
A bet placed behind a line or Come bet once a point is set. Pays true odds, so its house edge is 0%.
A payout that exactly matches the real chance of winning, such as 2:1 on a 4 or 10.
A common limit: up to 3x your flat bet on 4 and 10, 4x on 5 and 9, 5x on 6 and 8.
Like a Pass bet that starts on the next roll. It moves to a number and then wins if that number rolls before a 7.
The opposite of a Come bet. Wins when 7 comes before its number.
A bet that is working can win or lose on the next roll. Odds on Come bets are off on a come-out by default.
A bet that a number (4, 5, 6, 8, 9 or 10) rolls before a 7. Pays a little less than true odds.
A bet at true odds with a 5% commission. Best on 4 and 10, and best bought for $20 or more.
The opposite of a buy bet: betting a 7 will come before a number. Pays true odds minus 5% of the win.
The casino's commission on buy and lay bets. Also called juice.
A one-roll bet on 2, 3, 4, 9, 10, 11 or 12. In the default rules 2 and 12 pay double.
Even-money bets that 6 or 8 rolls before a 7. Place 6 and 8 pay better.
A one-roll bet in the center of the table, such as Any 7 or Aces. High payouts, high edge.
Bets that a 4, 6, 8 or 10 comes as a pair before it comes easy or a 7 shows.
A one-roll center bet that the next roll is a 7. Pays 4 to 1.
A four-way one-roll bet on 2, 3, 11 and 12.
Table slang for 11.
Two sixes: a roll of 12.
Two ones: a roll of 2.
The money you set aside for a session.
How far real results swing around the average. High variance means big swings.
The smallest bet the table allows on line, Come, place and field bets.
The pace of the game, about 100 rolls an hour by default here. Used to turn an edge into an hourly cost.
